name: Intelligent Claims Triage
subSegment: auto / P&C insurers, MGAs, third-party claims administrators
description: A working agent that automates first-notice-of-loss claims triage end to end: it extracts data from claim documents with Amazon Textract, cross-references coverage against policy documents in a Bedrock Knowledge Base, scores risk, and either auto-approves with a calculated payout or escalates to a human reviewer with policy-cited reasoning. Demo'd on auto insurance claims, the same extract → validate → score → route pattern drops into any document-heavy claims or intake workflow where auditability and human-in-the-loop escalation are non-negotiable.
buildLevelLabel: Custom IaC (CDK: AgentCore Runtime + API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB + Textract)
outcomes: 30–40% of low-risk claims auto-approved straight-through (vs. an industry STP baseline often under 10%), freeing adjusters for complex, high-value cases
Clean-claim cycle time cut from days to under 24 hours by automating document extraction and policy cross-referencing
~10–15 minutes of manual data entry and policy lookup eliminated per claim
Auditable, policy-cited rationale on every decision — auto-approval payout math and escalation reasons both persisted with the claim

roi.savings: $400K–800K/year (illustrative) in adjuster time from front-end automation + straight-through approval of low-risk claims
roi.cost: $25K–60K/year — Bedrock (Claude Haiku) + Amazon Textract pages + Knowledge Base (OpenSearch Serverless ~$350/mo floor) + Lambda / API Gateway / DynamoDB
roi.assumes: Illustrative: mid-size auto/P&C insurer, ~3,000 document-bearing claims/month, adjusters at ~$65/hr loaded doing manual extraction + policy lookup today (manual claim-doc handling runs $7–15/document industry-wide). Validate with your own numbers.

idealCustomer.size: Auto / P&C insurers, MGAs, and third-party claims administrators with high-volume, document-heavy first-notice-of-loss intake
idealCustomer.volume: 1,000+ claims/month arriving with supporting documents (repair estimates, police reports, photos); adjusters triaging manually today
idealCustomer.team: Claims operations team (adjusters plus a human-review / SIU function) supported by a small platform or engineering group
triggers: Adjusters spend hours keying data out of claim PDFs before they can even start adjudicating
Simple, low-value claims sit in the same queue as complex ones, inflating cycle time and customer wait
Leadership wants straight-through processing for low-risk claims but won't accept a black-box auto-approve
Compliance requires every automated decision to cite the specific policy terms it relied on
Policy documents already live in S3 or a document store but aren't usable for automated coverage checks
disqualifiers: Wants fully autonomous adjudication with no human in the loop on high-risk claims (this kit escalates by design)
Claims arrive as structured data only — no documents to extract (the Textract layer adds little value)
Requires on-premises or air-gapped deployment (kit is cloud-native AWS)
Sub-100 claims/month — automation overhead won't pay back

customerCustomizes: Risk-scoring rubric in the agent system prompt (`agent/claims_triage_agent.py`) — factor weights and the auto-approve vs. escalate threshold (default 0.7)
Policy corpus in the Bedrock Knowledge Base (`policy-docs/`) — replace the sample auto policy with your documents, or repoint `lookup_policy` at your policy system
Document extraction fields in `agent/tools/extract_document.py` — Textract form/line parsing tuned to your claim document formats
Payout calculation in the system prompt — `min(max(amount - deductible, 0), coverageLimit)` adjusted to your coverage rules
Claim intake schema and API contract in `lambda/submit-claim.js` plus the React intake views (`frontend/src/views/`)
Reviewer escalation in `agent/tools/notify_reviewer.py` (SQS queue + SNS topic) — point at your review tooling and notification channels
Optional Bedrock Guardrail (`GUARDRAIL_ID`) for PII redaction and topic boundaries on claim narratives
preBuilt: Strands triage agent on Bedrock AgentCore Runtime orchestrating 4 tools: extract document, lookup policy, update claim, notify reviewer
CDK (TypeScript) stack: API Gateway REST API with API key + usage plan, 8 Node.js Lambdas, DynamoDB claims table with status and policyNumber GSIs, two S3 buckets, SQS review queue, SNS topic
Async triage pattern — orchestrator Lambda returns 202 immediately, worker Lambda invokes AgentCore with a 5-minute budget
Amazon Textract extraction tool with FORMS/TABLES parsing plus text and raw-PDF fallbacks (`agent/tools/extract_document.py`)
Bedrock Knowledge Base policy-lookup tool that gracefully falls back to demo policy data when no KB is configured
React (Vite) demo UI with Adjuster, Customer, and Reviewer dashboards (`frontend/`)
Agent IAM execution-role policy template (`agent/agent-permissions-policy.template.json`) and sample claim + policy documents for smoke testing
sharedResponsibility: This kit is an accelerator and a working reference, not a managed service. Once deployed, you own the agent, the claims data, the policy corpus, the AWS infrastructure, and the human-review workflow in your own account. You and your engineering team adapt the risk rubric, policy Knowledge Base, and extraction fields to your claim formats. Scripts are provided as-is; partners can offer managed support engagements if needed.
